Team Description: Ingenious TEAM

Who are we? We are Ingenious TEAM, a group passionate about educational robotics, technology, and space exploration. We turn innovative ideas into real solutions for NASA challenges.

Our interests and skills:

Educational Robotics & Hardware: Development with microcontrollers (Arduino, ESP32, Micro:bit) and tech kits.

Programming & Software: Creation of applications, interfaces, and interactive tools.

STEM Approach: Integration of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics into practical projects.
summary:
To answer the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, the Ingenious TEAM developed an innovative educational and outreach platform that transforms NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars into fascinating historical treasures.

The solution addresses the challenge through digital storytelling and handcrafted audiovisual production. Its uniqueness lies in a co-creation process where young creators bring space exploration to life frame by frame using stop-motion animation, scale papercraft models, and detailed LEGO brick replicas of rovers, modules, and probes.

This project is essential because it fosters the social appropriation of science. By turning what many consider "space junk" into valuable scientific relics, it stimulates critical thinking and creativity, bringing the history of space exploration to children, youth, and adults in an engaging, educational, and unforgettable way.
details:
Project Details: "Abandoned but not Forgotten"

1. What does it do or how does it work?

The platform operates as an interactive digital storytelling and science outreach space. Its core consists of a series of audiovisual productions that narrate the missions, histories, and discoveries behind the artifacts, rovers, and modules abandoned by NASA on the Moon and Mars.

  • The Production Process: Instead of relying solely on generic digital animations, all content is handcrafted and co-created by the team.
  • Techniques: Frame-by-frame stop-motion animation is used to give movement to vehicles and astronauts across physical, handmade sets. This is combined with scale papercraft models (for probes, golden records, and heat shields) and detailed LEGO brick replicas (recreating iconic pieces like the Perseverance rover, the Ingenuity helicopter, and lunar modules).

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • Educational and Playful: Translates complex scientific concepts and historical space data into entertaining and accessible stories for all audiences, especially children and youth.
  • Fostering Creative and Citizen Science: By demonstrating how space models can be built using everyday materials (paper and building blocks), it encourages viewers to actively engage in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) projects.
  • Shift in Perspective: Transforms the negative concept of "space junk" or "waste" into a vision of heritage, historical, and scientific value regarding humanity's legacy on other worlds.

3. What is the expected impact of the project?

  • Inspiration and STEAM Vocations: Sparking interest in space exploration, engineering, and astronomy among new generations.
  • Community and Reach: Consolidating an educational digital community where users not only consume content but also feel motivated to create their own narratives using accessible tools.
  • Valuation of Extraterrestrial Heritage: Raising awareness about the historical importance of preserving and remembering the technological milestones resting on celestial bodies.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used to develop your project?

  • Hardware: Cameras and mobile devices for capturing stop-motion frames, tripods, and homemade studio lighting.
  • Editing and Animation Software: Stop-motion capture software (such as Dragonframe or specialized mobile apps), video editing software (such as Adobe Premiere or DaVinci Resolve), and graphic design tools for creating papercraft templates.
  • Physical Materials (Analog Hardware): LEGO building blocks, heavy-duty paper, cardstock, color printers, recycled materials, and physical textures to recreate lunar and Martian landscapes (craters, rocks, cosmic dust).

5. In what way is your project creative?

The creativity of the project lies in its hybrid approach between the handcrafted and the digital. In a technological environment saturated with computer-generated imagery (CGI) or artificial intelligence, the Ingenious TEAM bets on the warmth of hands-on work. Seeing a Mars rover built piece by piece with LEGO blocks or a space probe assembled millimeter by millimeter in paper moving frame by frame generates a unique, nostalgic, and deeply original emotional bond with the audience.

6. What factors did your team take into account?

  • Scientific and Historical Rigor: Despite using artisanal methods, each model (Papercraft and LEGO) and scripted story was based on actual technical specifications of NASA missions.
  • Accessibility and Sustainability: Demonstrating that expensive laboratories or high-end tools are not required to produce high-impact science communication; the materials used are low-cost and easy to acquire.
  • Emotional Connection: Designing narratives that not only convey hard data but also humanize space exploration, telling the "life stories" of these equipment left behind, solitary yet immortal on other worlds.
